Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexGen Security Platforms Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Participants are reminded that questions must be submitted via the Q&A tool in the webcast interface. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NexGen Security Platforms' results for the third quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Security Officer; and Taylor Kim, VP of Sales.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. NexGen Security Platforms continues to demonstrate leadership in the cybersecurity market. We achieved record bookings in the third quarter, driven by strong demand for our integrated NexSecure security platform and our expanding global presence. The positive customer feedback about NexSecure GenAI Shield and the resulting improvements in threat detection and response times is very encouraging.

We are focused on six strategic priorities that are fueling our momentum: accelerating platform adoption over legacy point products, expanding average deal sizes for both new and existing customers, enhancing channel partner performance and their revenue contribution, proving the effectiveness of our go-to-market strategy, scaling the number of new customers acquired, and providing clear next-quarter billings guidance to underscore our subscription momentum.

These priorities are not just goals—they're delivering tangible results in a market grappling with escalating threats, regulatory pressures, and the need for consolidated security platforms. Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. We delivered another quarter of strong financial results. Total revenue for the third quarter was $520 million, representing a 42% increase year-over-year. We saw significant growth in our subscription revenue, which now accounts for 85% of our total revenue. Gross margin was 84%, while operating expenses were $285 million. Net income was $112 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.78. We are reiterating our full-year guidance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial objectives.

As we dive deeper into the financials, I'd like to focus on one of the most critical dynamics driving our outperformance this quarter: the accelerating shift in customer adoption from legacy point products to our unified NexSecure Platform. This transition represents a structural change in the cybersecurity landscape, fueled by escalating threats, regulatory pressures, and the economic imperative for consolidation.

In Q3, our platform adoption rate—defined as the percentage of new Annual Recurring Revenue booked under the NexSecure Platform suite—reached 68%, up from 52% in Q3 2023 and a sequential jump from 62% in Q2. This marks the sixth straight quarter of acceleration. Conversely, point product bookings—our standalone offerings like legacy EDR modules or next-gen firewalls—fell to 22% of new ARR, down from 38% a year ago. The remaining 10% are hybrid transitions, where customers start with a point solution but commit to platform migration within 12 months via our Platform Path incentive program.

Our total ARR grew 42% year-over-year to $1.82 billion, with platform ARR surging 61% to $1.35 billion. This growth is value-driven, with the average Annual Contract Value for a new platform logo at $1.42 million—3.2 times higher than point products at $440,000. Net Retention Rate on platform customers hit 128%, compared to 112% for point-only accounts, thanks to seamless upsell paths into modules like Cloud Workload Protection, Secure Access Service Edge, and our AI-powered Extended Detection and Response layer.

Customers are moving away from the point product proliferation trap. Enterprises now manage an average of 47 security tools, up from 30 in 2020, leading to alert fatigue up 35% per our surveys and $4.5 million average annual tool sprawl costs. Following breaches like Change Healthcare ransomware and Snowflake credential stuffing, CISOs prioritize converged platforms for single-pane-of-glass visibility and orchestrated response. Our NexSecure Platform, with its hyperscale data lake ingesting 50 petabytes daily across EDR, NDR, and deception tech, reduces mean time to respond by 67% versus point silos, as validated by our 100% detection across 12 tactics in the latest MITRE ATT&CK evaluation.

On the technical side, Q3 saw general availability of NexSecure GenAI Shield, our agentless module for securing large language models against prompt injection and data exfiltration—already at 8% of new platform bookings. We've integrated zero-trust network access natively with our SASE stack, partnering with Zscaler for multi-tenant segmentation, boosting win rates against Prisma Access by 22% in head-to-head evaluations. R&D spend rose 18% year-over-year to $285 million, or 22% of revenue, funding autonomous SOAR that automates 85% of low-severity incidents amid a 25% global SOC analyst shortage.

Regionally, North America at 72% of ARR saw 75% platform adoption, including a $28 million expansion with a major U.S. bank migrating from CrowdStrike point modules to full XDR+SASE. EMEA hit 62% adoption, up 15 points, with 14 deals over €10 million, including a telco ditching Check Point firewalls. APAC/PAC reached 48% from 32%, with 87% ARR growth, including six $2.1 million deals in India. LatAm is at 35%, but pilots with Banco Itaú show promise.

This positions us for margin expansion—platform gross margins at 89% versus 82% for points. We expect platforms to be 80%+ of new ARR by FY25 end, with module penetration rising from 4.2 to 6.1 per customer. Our 1.2 billion endpoint coverage and zero-config CNAPP make us competitive.

Before moving on, another key indicator is average deal size, segmented by new logos and existing customers, highlighting our land-and-expand strategy amid threats, regulations, and cloud migrations.

New customer average ACV was $512,000, up 28% year-over-year from $400,000 and 8% sequentially from Q1. Driven by a 45% surge in ransomware, our NexusXDR 2.0 bundles EDR, NDR, and CWP—62% of new logos adopted the full suite. North America averaged $580,000 from financials seeking zero-trust; EMEA $490,000 via DORA; APAC $445,000 post-Change Healthcare.

Existing customer ACV was $378,000, up 18% YoY, with 122% NRR. Expansions included AI Guardian in 71% of deals, adding $95,000 ACV with 92% false positive reduction; DLP in 45%; multi-year deals at 3.2 years TCV $1.42 million. APAC expansions $410,000; EMEA $365,000; North America $390,000 via Azure co-sell.

Blended average $462,000, up 24% YoY, outpacing peers, reducing MTTR to under 15 minutes.

Channel partners are another cornerstone, accounting for 58% of our $520 million revenue, or $302 million, up 28% YoY and outpacing overall growth. Trailing 12-month partner revenue is 56% of $1.82 billion ARR. Active partners over 4,200, up 15%; platinum at 185, up 22%. Channel ACV $1.2 million, renewals 98%.

Americas 62% at $187 million, up 25% via Ingram Micro; EMEA $75 million up 35% via Arrow; APAC $40 million up 22% via TD SYNNEX. PartnerSync 2.0 certified 1,200 engineers, boosting large deals 40%; co-sell with CrowdStrike and Palo Alto added $15 million. Investments target 30% recurring managed services by FY25.

We added 1,847 new customers, up 28% YoY, totaling over 18,500. Enterprise 162 up 35%, ACV $450,000; mid-market/SMB 1,685 up 26%. North America 961 up 32%; EMEA 517 up 42%; APAC 369 up 15%. Driven by GenAI Threat Copilot, ecosystem, verticalization.

For Q4 billings, we guide $278 million to $288 million, up 11-15% sequentially, 22-27% YoY, affirming full-year $1.15-$1.18 billion. Cloud Security $125-130M; Endpoint/XDR $98-102M; Network/SASE $55-56M. Americas $172-179M; EMEA $67-69M; APAC $39-40M. Reflects GenAI Shield, R&D, amid ransomware surge.

Now, over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for technology updates.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Jordan. Our engineering team is laser-focused on innovation and delivering cutting-edge security solutions. We are leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance our threat detection and response capabilities. Key areas include advancing our NexSecure Platform with GenAI Shield for LLM security, autonomous SOAR for 85% incident automation, zero-config CNAPP, and hyperscale data lake analytics achieving 100% MITRE detection. These innovations are central to our platform adoption acceleration and upsell paths.

Marcus Hale: Security remains our top priority. We constantly monitor the threat landscape—from ransomware like LockBit to AI-driven attacks and nation-state APTs—and adapt our posture to protect customers and infrastructure. Our zero-trust integrations and threat intel feeds ensure resilience across endpoints, cloud, and networks.

Taylor Kim: Thank you. We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is executing well on land-and-expand, with 142 net new logos including Fortune 500 wins, 42% enterprise win rates, and pipeline at $1.8 billion up 75% YoY. Expanding channel partnerships to 62% of bookings reaches wider audiences effectively.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. First question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Chen: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On platform adoption, can you elaborate on regional differences and how GenAI Shield is contributing?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Mike. As Jordan detailed, platform adoption hit 68% overall, with North America at 75% from Fortune 500 consolidations like our U.S. bank deal, EMEA at 62% via NIS2, and APAC accelerating to 48%. GenAI Shield is at 8% of bookings already, securing LLMs against prompt injection—customers love the agentless deployment and MITRE-validated efficacy, driving upsells.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Patel: Great, thanks. Regarding average deal sizes, what are the key drivers for expansions, and any guidance update?

Jordan Lee: Hi Lisa. New ACV $512k up 28%, expansions $378k up 18%. Expansions driven by AI Guardian attach at 71%, DLP cross-sell, and 3.2-year terms. Q4 billings guide unchanged at $278-288M, with 20-25% YoY new logo growth expected.

Operator: Next question comes from David Ruiz with JPMorgan.

David Ruiz: Thanks. On channel performance, how is PartnerSync impacting large deals, and EMEA outlook?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: David, PartnerSync certified 1,200 engineers, yielding 40% more $2M+ deals via AWS/Azure integrations. EMEA up 35% YoY on NIS2, with Arrow/Westcon co-selling ZTNA—expect continued momentum with hyperscaler ramps.

Operator: Next question comes from Emma Wong with Barclays.

Emma Wong: Congrats. New customer adds are impressive—breakout verticals and competitive positioning?

Marcus Hale: Thanks, Emma. 1,847 adds, with healthcare up 45%, manufacturing 38%, infra 29%. Our GenAI Copilot outperforms legacy SIEMs, and channel/MSSP scale via Ingram gives us edge over point players—NRR 118% proves stickiness.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for cybersecurity solutions. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
